already_done_by_the_chat_lane.note: js/chat.js was rewritten by the chat lane between this lane's audit and its spec (mtime 2026-08-13 12:35, 989 -> 1029 lines). It now carries its own t(key, params, fallback) helper at js/chat.js:104 which prefixes 'local-looksmax-chat.forum.' and calls window.lmxI18n.t. All 23 static forum keys plus the seven dynamic api.* keys it asks for are exactly the key names in locale/en.yml and locale/es.yml here; verified key-by-key, zero missing and zero extra. No replacement is emitted for any of them.
also_already_localised: full() at js/chat.js:163 now composes lmxI18n.rel() + lmxI18n.date(), so the <time> title attribute no longer falls through to the BROWSER locale via toLocaleString().
paintPresence() at js/chat.js:495 now joins the member list with lmxI18n.list(), so it is "ana, beto y carla" rather than an English comma list.

replacements.note: The one string-shaped thing left in this file after the chat lane's own i18n pass. Layout was checked, not assumed: .LmxChat-time is `flex: none` (less/forum.less:286) inside a `display:flex` .LmxChat-meta, and .LmxChat-who beside it is `flex: 0 1 auto` with overflow:hidden + text-overflow:ellipsis (less/forum.less:271-279). A wider timestamp therefore shortens the username with an ellipsis and cannot break the row. If it turns out to shorten it too much, the fix belongs in looksmax-i18n rather than here: lmxI18n.rel() builds its formatter with { numeric: 'auto' } at js/dist/forum.js:148, and adding style: 'narrow' there gives "hace 2 min" / "2 min. ago" everywhere at once.
Guarded the same way t() already is, so it is safe wherever t() is. Apply before the two call sites below.
The presence count. Small today, but it is the one number in the card that a reader compares at a glance.
Characters remaining, counts down from 400 — three digits, so grouping never applies, but String() is still the wrong call to leave in place next to translated text.

Audit missed it. Every `detail` in this method is member-facing: failSend() at js/chat.js:728 does t('api.' + j.error, {max: S.maxLength}, j.detail) — it prefers the client-side key and falls back to this server string for a refusal it has not heard of. So the server text is the fallback for the client's own key set and must say the same thing in the same language. ChatController is built by the router with two injected dependencies; resolve() is used rather than widening its constructor, which is not this lane's file to change.
The only one of the seven that interpolates. The client passes {max: S.maxLength} for the same key, so the placeholder name has to be `max` on both sides — it is.
